justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term outlook on whatever underlying asset this forecast covers, with prices drifting gradually higher from roughly 344.5 at the one-day horizon to 350 at the one-month horizon. The one-day estimate was anchored primarily to recent price action and momentum, assuming no major overnight catalyst would materially disrupt the prevailing trend. The one-week estimate nudges slightly higher, reflecting a mild continuation bias where I expected modest drift in the direction of the near-term trend without assuming any sharp reversal or acceleration. The one-month estimate extends that drift further, essentially extrapolating a slow, steady grind higher while accounting for mean-reversion tendencies that tend to dampen extreme moves over longer windows.

The confidence interval widths widen substantially as the horizon extends, which is consistent with how uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 21 points, reflecting relatively tight short-run predictability where intraday volatility is the primary driver of spread. By one week, the interval nearly doubles to about 40 points, incorporating the possibility of scheduled macro events, earnings releases, or shifts in market sentiment that could arrive unexpectedly. At one month, the interval balloons to 80 points, acknowledging that a full month introduces exposure to a wide range of fundamental and technical developments that are genuinely difficult to anticipate.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data, an unexpected tightening of financial conditions, or a geopolitical shock could easily push the asset below 310 at the monthly horizon. Liquidity events or forced selling in correlated markets could amplify any initial move. On the upside, a surprise dovish pivot from a major central bank, a significant positive earnings or economic surprise, or a short-squeeze dynamic could drive prices well above 390. These tail scenarios are precisely why the intervals are stated at 90% rather than 99% — the remaining 10% of outcomes represents genuinely hard-to-model discontinuities that standard volatility scaling tends to underweight.
